title: Reading two essays about phones and driving to identify their points of agreement
summary: Students read two opposing essays on using phones while driving and determine which statements correctly reflect whether the writers agree on hands-free use, distraction, navigation apps, and penalties.

title: An inspiring article about an Iraqi Paralympic athlete's journey to international competition
summary: An article about Najla Imad Lafta, an Iraqi girl who lost her right arm and both legs in a car bomb at age three, who later discovered table tennis at ten, trained tirelessly, and earned a place on the Iraqi Paralympic team at twelve.

title: Unit 1 revision covering health vocabulary, past tenses, phrasal verbs, and linking phrases
summary: A revision page asking students to discuss and give further examples of key skills practised in Unit 1: describing minor health problems, telling stories with past simple and past continuous, using phrasal verbs, talking about past habits with used to, and organising ideas with linking phrases.

title: Opening page of Unit 2
summary: The introductory page for Unit 2 with no content beyond page layout and file information.

title: Unit 2 contents listing topics from law and order through security technology
summary: A contents overview for Unit 2 listing the following topics to be covered: Law and order, a police officer's duties, airport security, applying for a job, military jobs, a robbery, a safety brochure, road safety, security technology, and Round up.

title: Law and order vocabulary matching exercise with photos and a listening task
summary: Students match vocabulary items such as footprint, fingerprint, radar speed gun, metal detector, X-ray machine, security camera, crime scene, speed limit, and security guard with corresponding photos, then listen to a conversation identifying the speakers as a police officer or a driver.

title: Exploring a police officer's duties through brainstorming and reading an information pack
summary: Students first brainstorm activities a police officer performs with a partner, then read extracts from an information pack given in a police officer's school talk covering duties like directing traffic, using speed guns, checking seat belts, and investigating crimes to compare with their own ideas.

title: Airport security procedures with listening tasks and functional language practice
summary: Students examine photos of airport locations visited before boarding and after landing, listen to a conversation checking their ideas, and then classify dialogue sentences as polite requests, suggestions, advice, or offers to practise functional language used in airport settings.
